topics.topic: Actions that count as using the photo folder and trigger validation
questions: Which concrete actions constitute use of the photo folder and must perform the outside-root check?
Which actions count as using the photo folder: connecting, confirming, listing deliverables, placing a photo, or some combination of them?
Which promised action constitutes using the linked photo folder and must perform the refusal?

quotes:
Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects.
judgement.why: State 2 specifies that scan and placement are the uses that perform the resolved-containment check, while connection loading and marking do not perform it.

topics.topic: Exact normalization and containment rule for written subfolder paths
questions: Which written subfolder forms count as leaving the root, and is the decision made before or after normalization, decoding, separator conversion and case handling?
What exact written subfolder forms count as leaving the root, and is containment decided before or after path normalization?
What exact path-containment rule determines that a written subfolder leaves its root?

quotes:
The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself.
judgement.why: State 2 defines the accepted written form directly, rejecting every subfolder containing `..` rather than deciding from a normalized destination.

topics.topic: Filesystem indirections and canonical root used to determine an outside-root link
questions: What kinds of indirection count as being linked outside the root, and what filesystem identity establishes that the final target is outside?

Which indirections make a photo folder 'linked outside': the final folder being a symbolic link, a link in any ancestor, hard links, junctions, bind mounts, or a root that is itself linked elsewhere; and against which canonical root is 'outside' measured?
What identifies the root for containment: the configured path text, the normalized absolute path, or the filesystem object reached after resolving links?
Which links count, and where in the path must they occur for the folder to be treated as linked outside the root?

quotes:
Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.

Ignored names are
not reported, ignored folders are not entered, and symbolic links are neither reported nor followed.
judgement.why: State 2 measures containment between the resolved folder and resolved root and separately forbids following symbolic links encountered during traversal.

topics.topic: Persistent connection state after an outside-root refusal
questions: After this refusal, does the connection remain confirmed and usable if the link is repaired, or is confirmation revoked or another persistent failure state recorded?

May a connection whose photo folder currently links outside the root be stored or confirmed despite delivery being refused when the folder is used, and if so does a later refusal invalidate that connection?
After the refusal, what happens to the confirmed connection record and its claim that delivery is possible?

quotes:
A change of an object's root or subfolder writes `assignment_confirmed` false (R0-11). An
   operation on a project with no connection is refused with `unknown_project`, and one with an
   unconfirmed connection with `connection_not_confirmed`. This is decided by the service, not by
   the caller.

Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
judgement.why: State 2 makes confirmation clearing a consequence of changing the configured root or subfolder, whereas an outside-root resolution only refuses that scan or placement, so repairing the filesystem permits a retry without reconfirmation.

topics.topic: Race-safe validation when link targets change during use
questions: Must the implementation prevent the folder or any ancestor from being retargeted outside the root between validation and file access, and which filesystem operation provides that guarantee?

If the folder or an ancestor changes into an outside-root link after validation or while an operation is running, at what point must the operation refuse access and what happens to work already completed?
At what moments must containment be checked, and what must happen if the link target changes between checking and opening a file?

quotes: | Connect an object to its folders (owner, through the agent) | a connection record the owner has confirmed; delivery becomes possible for that project | a connection whose subfolder is written to leave its root is refused, a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used, and an unconfirmed connection delivers nothing | unit tests |
judgement.why: The moments and race-safety mechanism of containment enforcement are operation rules and required-test matters owned by State 2 rather than State 0 product-boundary questions.

topics.topic: Scope of the operation or files refused after outside-root detection
questions: Does detection refuse the whole operation, only the affected folder, only the affected file, or the connection itself?
What is refused and what observable result is returned: the whole project operation, the affected folder, or individual files, and what status or reason does the owner receive?
Does discovery of an outside link refuse the entire project operation, only that folder, or only the affected file, and may unaffected files proceed?

quotes:
Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.

When a subfolder that is not ignored
cannot be listed, the whole operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`, so a partial scan is
never reported as complete.
judgement.why: State 2 defines outside-root containment failure as refusal of the operation with `folder_unavailable` and rules out a partial scan result.

topics.topic: Atomicity and permitted side effects when an outside link is discovered mid-operation
questions: When the outside link is discovered during listing or placement, which records or files, if any, may already have been written, and must the operation leave everything unchanged?
If the outside link is discovered after an operation has begun, must the operation leave all state unchanged, or may results already produced for unaffected files remain?

quotes:
A call holds from 1 to 50 source ids, otherwise it is refused whole. Checks run in this order:
   token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, every source id.

Items are processed in request order, so
   a source id repeated in one call is `placed` and then `replayed`. A read or storage failure of
   one photo is reported in its item as `unreadable_file` and the others proceed.
judgement.why: State 2 places the photo-folder containment check before every source item and every write, while failures encountered during subsequent per-item processing preserve completed unaffected items and allow the others to proceed.

topics.topic: Observable refusal status, reason, and recipient
questions: What observable result identifies each refusal to the owner or calling flow, including whether the two failures have distinct stable reasons?
What observable output reports this refusal, including its reason and the actor that receives it?

quotes:
The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself. Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
There is one principal: the calling flow of the owner. It may act on every confirmed connection.

`RefusalCode` is `unknown_project`,
`connection_not_confirmed`, `folder_unavailable`, `invalid_source_id`, `unsafe_reference`,
`not_placed` and `publication_conflict`.
judgement.why: State 2 gives both invalid written subfolders and resolved outside-root folders the stable `folder_unavailable` refusal seen by the owner's calling flow, so they are not distinct refusal codes.

topics.topic: Whether connection may succeed when the photo folder already resolves outside the root
questions: Can connecting and confirming a photo folder that already links outside the root report success even though delivery through it will be refused, or must connection fail so that “delivery becomes possible” remains true?
May the Connect action confirm and store a connection whose photo folder already resolves outside the root, or must Connect refuse it immediately as well?

quotes:
Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects.

The agent writes the connection for a project the Registry already
issued, and sets the confirmation only for the folders the owner confirmed.

The deliverer only reads the
connection.
judgement.why: The later texts permit the agent to store and confirm a lexically valid connection without resolving its photo folder, because resolved containment is checked only by each later scan or placement.

topics.topic: Whether outside-root protection applies to roots and non-photo folders
questions: Are links outside the root permitted for the object's other folders, or must the same use-time boundary rule apply to every connected folder?
Does outside-root link protection apply only to the photo folder, or also to the root itself and every other connected folder used by the project?

quotes:
Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.

The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so
   the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record
   (R0-09).
judgement.why: State 2 compares the photo folder with the resolved root and assigns resolved-containment checking of the invoice folder to the Cabinet Inbox when that folder is used.

topics.topic: Failure-reason precedence when outside-link detection overlaps another failure
questions: When an outside link also makes the folder unavailable or makes a selected file differ from the scanned file, which promised failure and reason takes precedence?

quotes:
Inside the call the folder is scanned once. A requested source with no placement that this scan
   does not report as `ready` fails with `not_ready_or_absent`. A source reported `ready` whose
   bytes no longer have the requested hash when it is read for placing fails with `source_changed`.

Checks run in this order:
   token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, every source id.

Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
judgement.why: State 2 checks and refuses an unavailable outside-root photo folder before examining source ids, so `folder_unavailable` takes precedence over the later `source_changed` check.
